lead: The whole-page frame: where the header, navigation, tab bar, content and footer go is chosen by `layout`, one of five: side, top, mix, column and boxed. It is data-driven and knows nothing about routes: the navigation is a tree (`items`) plus the current item (`activeKey`), clicks come back through `onNavigate`, and you navigate in the callback. Put [PageTabs](/page-tabs) in the tab bar and [KeepAlive](/keep-alive) around the content and you have the console's setup; on narrow screens the sidebar becomes a drawer, and the top / mix / column navigation moves into a menu button in the header.

usage.title: Usage
usage.description: Switch the layout above to see the five arrangements. Clicking the navigation opens a tab, and `KeepAlive` keeps each page's state; in mix / column, clicking a top-level item goes to its first child and the menu below shows its children. Narrow the browser window to try the narrow-screen version.

maximized.title: Collapsed and maximized
maximized.description: `collapsed`: the sidebar collapses to an icon-only strip (in column, the level-2 menu column collapses); `maximized`: the header, sidebar and navigation are hidden, leaving only the tabs, content and footer.

customize.title: Customize
customize.description: The `AdminLayoutSettings` panel edits a settings object (layout, menu / tab style, colors, radius, density), and AdminLayout's `settings` (its `themeOverrides`) turns the colors and radius into CSS variables. Pick a preset first, then try changing single colors: a dark background makes the text, border and neutral colors follow; a dark sidebar color makes the menu text light. The theme here only applies inside the preview (`themeScope` defaults to `layout`); to make overlays such as menus and dialogs follow too, pass `themeScope="document"`.

nav.title: Navigation items
nav.label: The text shown
nav.icon: Leading icon; all that's left when the sidebar collapses to a strip and in the column layout's icon rail
nav.href: When given, the item renders as a link `<a>`; to navigate yourself, call `preventDefault()` in `onNavigate`
nav.titleField: Tooltip text and accessible name when only the icon shows; may be omitted when `label` is a string
nav.children: Child items. The top layout's dropdowns show two levels; the sidebar / drawer can go deeper; in mix / column the top-level items' children are the content of the sidebar / level-2 menu

helpers.title: Helpers
helpers.trailOf: The whole path from the top level to `key` (including itself)
helpers.firstLeaf: Follows the first enabled child down to a leaf (where clicking a top-level item with children goes)
helpers.activeTopOf: The top-level item the current item belongs to; the first one when it isn't in the navigation

styling.title: Styling Reference
styling.logo: The brand; in the sidebar, `logo-mark` shows only when the sidebar is collapsed to a strip (instead of the logo)
styling.nav: The top-level navigation of top / mix; `nav-item` has `data-active`
styling.rail: The column layout's icon rail; `rail-item` has `data-active`
styling.subnav: The column layout's level-2 menu column and its collapse button (`data-collapsed`)
styling.main: The main area: the tab row (`bar`), content, footer (`data-fixed`)
styling.bar: The built-in refresh and maximize / restore buttons on the right of the tab row
styling.drawer: The full navigation in the narrow-screen drawer

shell.slotsHint: Every one of these is an optional slot — leave it out and nothing is rendered.
shell.customizeHint: Layout, colors, radius and density. Everything is plain data — save it wherever you like.
